# Independent audit: residual exit stopping and critical overshoot


`candidate 3f94bc936c5d4a14`
against its archived tiny-contained-endpoint depth dependency.

This is an auxiliary inequality and obstruction, not OC.

1. The positive residual projection is convex. Along a segment between
positive original fibers, actual compact fibers are Hausdorff continuous,
including at its endpoints: compactness gives upper continuity; combining
any endpoint point with a fixed point on the other side gives lower
continuity. A negative margin point in a full-dimensional convex fiber
implies positive residual volume by mixing with an interior ball. Thus
first exit has minimum margin zero, a nonempty closed contact section,
and zero full-dimensional volume. No empty set is inserted into BM.

2. With b_j=p+t_j(z_j-p), the proposed weights theta_j/(c t_j) have sum
one and barycenter p exactly. Weighted BM on these nonempty closed
residuals gives sum_positive theta_j f_j<=c f_p; the factors at positive
destinations equal one. This verifies both the displayed correction and
its geometric dependence. The real boundary bases b_j are auxiliary
only, not claimed mixed-integer centers.

3. In a KKT transition row, include the original stopping atom at p with
weight D_ii. The new total probability numerator is
sum_inside T_ij+D_ii+sum_outside T_ij/t_ij=c_i. The barycenter calculation
is identical. Since all retained D_ii>0 and there are finitely many
finite c_i, original stopping has a uniform positive conditional
probability. Hence the transient matrix has convergent geometric powers
and the displayed inverse/terminal matrix is justified. Its omitted mass
belongs to boundary stops of zero residual root, proving Wf<=f. There is
no substitution of the old terminal coupling for W.

4. In the critical A,T,T construction the displayed P caps capture all A,
a canonical middle cap, and no right fiber for L>=2; the Q caps capture
only a canonical right cap. All barycentric coordinate ranges lie in
[0,1], including the distinguished coordinate on A. The cover, residual
minima (0,c,c), constant optimal convex threshold, exact KKT multipliers,
and terminal row (1/3,1/3,1/3) are consistent.

5. The actual intermediate fiber at -t is
[1-(1-epsilon)t]T. Its relevant barycentric coordinate has minimum zero.
The residual for lambda_1-Lz>=1/(d+1) therefore vanishes exactly at
 t=1/((d+1)L). This proves the unbounded c_row with unchanged original
masses and transition data. Genuine global criticality uses the previously
proved all-halfspace tiny-endpoint theorem, not the displayed cap cover
alone. The normalized depth is explicitly above Gamma_d/2.

6. The conclusion is correctly restricted: criticality does not control
EVERY chosen cap's overshoot from the fixed listed data. The construction
does not rule out optimizing the critical-cap choice, a different stopping
rule, or a bound that additionally uses a strict below-target premise.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
